Title: Intel (INTC) Stock Closes at $43.63 as SambaNova AI Partnership Provides Lift Amid Ongoing Challenges

Summary: 
Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC) closed at $43.63 on Monday, February 23, 2026, a 1.09% decline from the prior session's $44.11, but rose about 1.4% in pre-market trading on Tuesday, February 24, to $44.24 following news of a multi-year technical partnership with AI chip startup SambaNova Systems. The deal includes Intel's participation in SambaNova's $350 million Series E funding round and a collaboration where SambaNova will adopt Intel server processors and graphics cards for its systems. Intel's market capitalization is approximately $217–220 billion, supported by cash reserves and CHIPS Act funding, but weighed down by ongoing foundry losses and competitive pressures in AI and data center chips. The stock traded in a 52-week range of $17.67 to $54.60, and is up roughly 18–20% year-to-date in 2026 from late-2025 levels, reflecting cautious optimism about new CEO Lip-Bu Tan’s turnaround strategy. However, the stock remains below its 2021 peak. Q1 2026 guidance projected revenue of $11.7–12.7 billion, below estimates, citing supply constraints and weak PC demand. Full-year 2025 results showed revenue growth but persistent foundry losses exceeding $2.5 billion annually. Management targets foundry breakeven by 2027–2028, with customer commitments for the 14A process expected in the second half of 2026. Analysts remain divided: consensus rating is Hold to Moderate Buy, with a 12-month price target of $45–48. Risks include delays in the Nova Lake CPU (pushed beyond CES 2027) and Meta’s shift toward Nvidia for some CPU workloads. Bulls highlight undervaluation, government support, and potential upside from foundry ramps and AI partnerships. Institutional activity shows mixed flows, with modest insider buying. The next major catalyst is Q1 2026 earnings (expected late April), where investors will assess foundry progress, AI GPU traction (Gaudi and Falcon Shores), and new customer wins. Intel remains a high-risk, high-reward turnaround story, dependent on execution in a competitive landscape dominated by Nvidia, AMD, and custom silicon players.

Published date: February 24 2026, 15:40

Source: International Business Times Australia
Classification: Finance
Sentiment: neutral
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: North America

Title: Is Intel Stock Going to $100?

Summary: 
Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) stock rose 84% in 2025 and gained 22% in 2026 despite a significant drop following its fourth-quarter 2025 results, which missed expectations due to supply-related challenges. CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated that supply constraints 'meaningfully limited' Intel's ability to meet strong demand in both the PC and data center markets, with the most acute issues expected in the current quarter. However, supply challenges are anticipated to ease starting in the next quarter, and chip production yields are improving. Intel's revenue from custom artificial intelligence (AI) processors grew 50% year over year in the prior quarter, achieving an annualized run rate of over $1 billion, with shipments expected to triple by 2027 compared to 2024 levels. Analysts project a 15% earnings increase in 2026 to $0.48 per share, with earnings growth accelerating into 2028. Assuming Intel reaches $1.40 per share in earnings by 2028 and trades at a 50x earnings multiple—justified by its high growth—the stock could reach $70. While Intel stock currently trades at around $46 per share, making a $100 target unlikely in the near term, the company's cost-cutting, improving yields, and expanding AI chip business provide strong catalysts for continued growth.

Published date: February 27 2026, 23:05

URL: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/intel-stock-going-100
Source: NASDAQ Stock Market
Classification: Finance
Sentiment: positive
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: North America

Title: Intel (INTC) Stock: Is It a Buy Ahead of Thursday’s Earnings?

Summary: 
Intel (INTC) is set to report Q4 2025 earnings on Thursday, January 22, after market close, with analysts forecasting EPS of $0.08—a 38.5% year-over-year decline—and revenue of $13.40 billion, down 6% YoY. The stock, which surged 116–145% in 2025, is trading near its 52-week high of $50.39 at $48.32. Wall Street maintains a consensus Hold rating, based on eight Buy, 19 Hold, and four Sell ratings, with an average price target of $43.37, implying a 7.64% downside. Jefferies raised its price target to $45 from $40 while keeping a Hold, citing improving server demand but warning of production capacity constraints due to shifting Intel 7/10 capacity from low-end PCs to legacy server products. The analyst expects PC market weakness starting in March, with declines of at least mid-single digits, and rising memory costs that may force manufacturers to cut specs or raise prices. Margin pressure is also a concern, with Jefferies projecting margins below 36%—a 200 basis point drop from December consensus—due to Lunar Lake and 18A process ramp-ups. Intel plans to insource 70% of Panther Lake manufacturing by Q1 2026, which may cause initial supply constraints. RBC Capital initiated coverage with a Sector Perform rating and $50 target, acknowledging progress on the balance sheet, the Nvidia partnership, and competitive product gains, but flagging Intel’s lack of a clear data center AI strategy and limited visibility in the foundry business, where delays persist. The company’s CEO met with President Donald Trump, who praised Intel’s new sub-2 nanometer CPU launch, and Mobileye announced a $900 million acquisition of Mentee Robotics, expected to close in early 2026.

Published date: January 19 2026, 10:00

Title: Intel (INTC) Stock: Shares Hit 52-Week High on Server Chip Shortage

Summary: 
Intel (INTC) shares surged 7.3% to a 52-week high of $47.29 on January 14, 2026, after KeyBanc upgraded the stock to Overweight with a $60 price target. Intel’s 18A manufacturing process now achieves yields above 60%, positioning the company as a potential second-largest global foundry, behind only TSMC. Apple is expected to begin using Intel’s foundry services for lower-end MacBook and iPad processors starting in 2027, with potential use of Intel’s 14A process for budget iPhone chips by 2029. AMD also received an Overweight upgrade from KeyBanc, with a $270 price target and expectations of at least 50% server CPU revenue growth in 2026. AMD’s AI GPUs, the MI355 and MI455, are projected to generate $14–15 billion in revenue, with 200,000 MI355 units expected to ship in H1 2026 and 290,000–300,000 MI455 units in H2 2026. Institutional ownership of Intel rose 6.13% quarter-over-quarter, with 3,082 funds holding shares. Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund owns 126.3 million shares (2.53% of Intel). Intel’s projected annual revenue is $100.9 billion, with non-GAAP EPS forecast at $3.56. The average analyst price target of $37.52 is below the current stock price, suggesting potential for upward revisions. The options market shows bullish sentiment, with a put/call ratio of 0.70.

Title: Intel (INTC) Stock: CES 2026 Showcases First 18A Process Chips as Analysts Upgrade Shares

Summary: 
Intel (INTC) unveiled its Panther Lake processor family at CES 2026, marking the company’s first chips built using its 18A manufacturing process. The Core Ultra Series 3 processors, produced in Intel’s own facilities, deliver a 60% performance improvement over the previous Lunar Lake chips and feature a new transistor architecture and dedicated graphics chiplet. The launch is critical for Intel as it seeks to regain market share from AMD. CEO Lip-Bu Tan confirmed the 18A products were shipped by the end of 2025. Intel plans to release a handheld gaming platform based on Panther Lake later in 2026, along with updated Arrow Lake processors and new Arc graphics cards such as the B770 model. Despite past concerns about manufacturing yields, executives stated that production quality improves monthly without impacting the launch timeline. Melius Research upgraded Intel stock to Buy with a $50 price target, citing potential foundry growth, particularly from future 14A process technology. Analyst Ben Reitzes speculated that Nvidia and Apple—both Intel shareholders—could become foundry customers by 2028–2029, potentially boosting Intel’s stock value through 2026. Intel shares have risen 98.19% over the past year. The stock currently has six Buy, 19 Hold, and six Sell ratings, with an average price target of $39. Meanwhile, AMD announced a major deal with OpenAI for MI400 processors, and Nvidia revealed next-generation AI chips in full production with five times more computing power than prior versions. Intel’s success with the 18A process will determine its ability to attract external foundry clients and strengthen its position in semiconductor manufacturing.

Published date: January 06 2026, 13:50

Reporting voice: Objective
Continent: North America

RBC Capital initiated coverage with a $50 target and Sector Perform rating, praising balance sheet improvements and product competitiveness but noting Intel’s lack of a clear AI data center strategy. The consensus rating is Hold, with an average target of $43.37, implying a 7.64% downside. Analysts expect a muted full-year outlook due to PC market softening starting in March, higher memory costs, and persistent capacity limitations. Intel plans to insource 70% of Panther Lake processor manufacturing by Q1 2026. The company’s foundry business remains unclear due to ongoing production delays. Mobileye announced a $900 million acquisition of Mentee Robotics, closing in early 2026. Intel’s CEO recently met with President Trump, who highlighted the upcoming sub-2 nanometer CPU launch.

articles.title: Intel Stock Rally Analysis: Can INTC Double in 2026?
articles.summary: Intel Corp (INTC) stock rallied approximately 84% in 2025 and remains up about 25% year-to-date in 2026, despite a pullback following weaker-than-expected Q1 projections. According to Barchart.com, for Intel stock to double in 2026, it would need to reach $73.8, implying a 54% upside from its recent closing price of $47.98. The company's growth is driven by AI data center tailwinds, with its Data Center and AI (DCAI) segment generating $4.7 billion in revenue in the fourth quarter, a 15% sequential increase. Management noted that revenue could have been higher if supply constraints had not limited output. Additionally, Intel's custom ASIC business grew more than 50% in 2025, reaching an annualized revenue run rate of over $1 billion in Q4. Despite positive trends in AI demand and supply normalization expected in Q2, Wall Street analysts maintain a consensus 'Hold' rating, with the highest price target at $66 per share, representing roughly 38% upside.
